title: The Strip in the Drawer
subtitle: 植物农业 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）
meta: 主题语境：植物农业（自然生态·植物与农业）　|　核心词汇：bark　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 bark 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1953 my grandfather stripped ① a bark from a fallen tree and kept it for eleven years in a drawer, and my grandmother said the keeping was the strange part. The ② bark, meaning the strip and not the tree, was used once, to mend a boot, and was never mentioned again; a bark, he said, is the only part of a tree that survives the tree by being useless.

Every ③ bark on that woodpile came from the same winter, and the ④ bark on the north side, meaning the thick one he never cut and not either of those, was still there in March when the pile was gone. A bark, my mother said, is nine parts habit and one part an excuse to go out; my grandmother said the habit is the part that lasts.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ bark was the whole of the dog, meaning the noise and not the skin. The ⑥ bark, meaning the sound and not any of that, is the only thing in a yard that everybody hears and nobody answers; a bark, he said, is either what you peel off a tree or the only argument an animal can start from a distance. She said the distance is the point.

By 1966 the ⑦ bark had become a word in an argument about the fence, and the argument had become a habit of its own. The ⑧ bark of the whole thing, my grandfather wrote in April, was eleven years in a drawer and one mended boot; a bark, he said, is either the skin of a tree or the reason the dog is useful. She said the dog was never useful.

The ⑨ bark I remember is the strip in the drawer, which was thrown out in 1969 by somebody who had not been told. A ⑩ bark, my mother said in 1971, is the only thing that improves by being kept too long; every bark, she said, is a tree that has agreed to look like a habit. He said the tree was the alibi.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: B. n. 树皮（指剥下来的那一条，与树相对）
C. 固定搭配：strip a bark 剥下一块树皮
D. n. 树皮（指木堆上每一块）
E. n. 树皮（指北侧那块厚的）
G. n. 吠声（抽象：那阵声音）
H. n. 权衡；整件事的分量（抽象总称）

items.q: a bark from a fallen tree
The bark, meaning the strip and not the tree
the bark on the north side
bark was the whole of the dog
the bark had become a word in an argument about the fence
The bark of the whole thing
A bark, my mother said in 1971

answers.why: strip a bark 意为“剥下一块树皮”，1953 年祖父从一棵倒下的树上剥下一块树皮，在抽屉里放了十一年。
bark 意为“树皮”，指剥下来的那一条而不是树，它只用过一次，用来补一只靴子。
bark 指木堆上每一块树皮，那个木堆上每一块都来自同一个冬天。
bark 指北侧那块厚的树皮（他从没砍过的那块），三月木堆没了它还在。
bark 意为“吠声、狗叫”，叔叔说 bark 就是那条狗的全部，指的是叫声而不是树皮。
bark 为抽象用法，指那阵声音，是院子里人人都听见、却没人回应的东西。
bark 意为“树皮”，到 1966 年这个 bark 成了一场关于篱笆的争吵里的一个词。
bark 意为“权衡、整件事的分量”，祖父四月写道，整件事权衡下来是在抽屉里放的十一年和一只补好的靴子。
bark 意为“树皮”，我记得的是抽屉里那一条，1969 年被一个不知情的人扔了。
bark 为抽象总称，母亲说树皮是唯一会因为放得太久才变好的东西。
